request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Code has already chosen the configuration to carry forward with a paired fold rule; the choice and the paired comparisons behind it are under 'selection'. Your job is to decide whether more search is worthwhile and to flag concerns, especially any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; propose configurations that could plausibly beat the current choice on paired folds, and set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. (Independent run 2, definitions.)

schema.description:
The choice of configuration is made in code (selection.py); the critic decides
whether to search further and flags concerns.

stop.description: true if no further experiment is justified
stop.title: Stop

schema.title: CriticVerdict

concerns: High ROC-AUC (~0.94) and PR-AUC (~0.73) on a Medicare fraud task suggest potential data leakage or utilization of proxy features.
Substantial fold-to-fold variance (PR-AUC standard deviation around 0.056, with fold scores ranging from 0.64 to 0.79) indicates model instability across data partitions.
Run 4 (Random Forest) was selected over Run 1 (LightGBM) despite a marginally lower mean PR-AUC, though performance between the two is statistically tied.
